newsitem.title: USA: Liberian leader asks U.S. to help peace process.
newsitem.headline: Liberian leader asks U.S. to help peace process.

text.p: Liberia's chief of state called on the Clinton administration on Friday to help prevent a return to civil war in her nation, which was founded by freed U.S. slaves.

"Time is not on our side and we have to act quickly if the peace process is to succeed," Ruth Perry, head of state and chairman of the Liberian National Transitional Government, told a news conference at the National Press Club.
She urged the United States to send financial and logistical support to help an African peacekeeping force deploy throughout Liberia, which has been devastated by civil war since December 1989.

Peacekeepers from Nigeria, Guinea, Ghana and other West African states, collectively known by the acronym ECOMOG, said this week they may have to use force against guerrillas loyal to Gen. Roosevelt Johnson, a factional leader.
The rebels known as the ULIMO-J militia have been blocking international food aid to western areas of Liberia, founded by freed slaves in 1847 as Africa's first independent republic.

Aides said Perry would meet Undersecretary of State Peter Tarnoff, the State Department's third-ranking official, and Susan Rice, the White House National Security Council director for international organisations and peacekeeping.
